subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Data in a hot storage tier is actively indexed and retrievable along many access paths; data in a cold storage tier is unindexed and can only be retrieved by sequential scan.
• In a warm tier, an outer indexed partition (the frame) encloses an inner partition of partially unindexed data blocks (the core) within a single volume.
• This warm tier was previously thought to be a temporary migration phase between the hot and cold tiers.
• A 2021 study by Nyala Mansour and Babatunde Benali confirmed that, even under heavy write loads, the frame remained fully indexed while the core never became fully unindexed.
• The core data blocks lost most access paths but retained one linear retrieval path enforced by the frame.
• The warm tier was determined to be a stable, distinct storage state.
prompt: The student wants to explain why data is not fully unindexed in a warm tier. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: A warm tier involves a dual partition of a fully indexed frame enclosing a core of partially unindexed data blocks.
choices.B: In a warm tier, some data blocks exhibit the unindexed character of cold storage but are held by the indexed frame to a single linear retrieval path, preventing the loss of all access paths that defines fully unindexed data.
choices.C: A 2021 study confirmed that data does not become fully unindexed under heavy write loads; instead, it enters a warm tier, a temporary migration phase between hot and cold storage.
choices.D: Because data in the warm tier loses most access paths even under heavy write loads, it cannot reach a fully unindexed state.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. This choice explains why data is not fully unindexed in a warm tier by identifying the key mechanism: some data blocks exhibit the disorder of cold storage (lost access paths) but remain confined by the indexed frame to a single linear retrieval path, preventing the complete loss of access paths that would characterize fully unindexed data.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. This choice reverses the causal relationship: it suggests that losing most access paths prevents data from becoming fully unindexed, but the notes indicate that losing access paths is actually a characteristic of the cold (unindexed) state. The correct explanation is that the indexed frame confines the core data to one retrieval path despite its lost access paths.
